Each referenced key must resolve into the bundle's global calc-key namespace and must be owned by this species entry (workflow-layer ownership check). |
| `torsions` | array of [`BundleStatmechTorsionIn`](#model-tckdb-schemas-workflows-computed-reaction-upload-bundlestatmechtorsionin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  | Torsional modes. |
| `energy_level_of_theory` | [`LevelOfTheoryRef`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-refs-leveloftheoryref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional depositor-declared level of theory the record's energy is claimed to stand at. See ``app.services.calculation_levels`` on the backend for the exact rule; never persisted. |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional note. |

Rules:

- **BundleStatmechIn.normalize_point_group** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **BundleStatmechIn.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - statmech.source_calculations must be unique by (calculation_key, role).

- **BundleStatmechIn.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Statmech torsion_index values must be unique within a species.

- **BundleStatmechIn.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

- **BundleTransitionStateIn.validate_reaction_coordinate_contract** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Refuse frequency evidence with no usable reaction coordinate.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). A transition state
  does not carry a ``stationary_point_kind`` — the entity is the
  claim — so this model is where the declaration and the evidence
  meet. ADR 0012 narrowed what is definitional here: not the
  *count* of imaginary modes, but that there is at least one, that
  exactly one is designated the reaction coordinate, and that no
  undeclared mode is stiff enough to make that designation
  meaningless.

- **BundleTransitionStateIn.validate_evidence_source_is_a_ts_irc_calculation** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Evidence must name an ``irc`` calculation owned by this TS.

  Participant/atom completeness needs the bundle's reaction, which this
  nested model cannot see; the enclosing request validates that.

Rules:

- **CalculationInBundle.validate_result_matches_type** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  One result block, matching ``type`` (mirrors
  ``CalculationWithResultsPayload.validate_result_matches_type``).

  ``scan_result`` is bundle-only — the primitive
  ``CalculationWithResultsPayload`` does not carry it; the bundle
  workflow persists it via ``persist_calculation_scan`` after the
  calculation row is created.

- **CalculationInBundle.validate_constraints** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Enforce constraint_index uniqueness across this calc.

  Top-level ``constraints`` and ``scan_result.constraints`` share the
  same ``calculation_constraint`` table at persistence time, so
  ``constraint_index`` must be unique across the union of both lists
  within one calculation.

- **CalculationInBundle.reject_database_id_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  DR-0029 Requirement 1: bundle must not carry DB FK ids.

  Walks ``parameters_json`` recursively to catch FK ids that would
  bypass the model's ``extra="forbid"`` (which only enforces
  structural keys, not opaque ``dict`` payloads).

### `ChebyshevKineticsIn`

`app.schemas.workflows.network_pdep_upload`. Used by: [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#surface-networkpdepuploadrequest).

Chebyshev-polynomial fit of a phenomenological k(T,P).

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Unit | Allowed values | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_temperature` | integer | yes |  |  |  | >= 1 | Number of temperature basis polynomials (rows). |
| `n_pressure` | integer | yes |  |  |  | >= 1 | Number of pressure basis polynomials (columns). |
| `coefficients` | array of array of number | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 | 2D coefficient grid, ``n_temperature`` rows each of length ``n_pressure``. Persisted as ``{"coeffs": [[...], ...]}`` JSONB to match the network-kinetics read path. |

Rules:

- **ChebyshevKineticsIn.validate_grid_dimensions** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Chebyshev coefficients must have n_temperature={self.n_temperature} rows, got {len(self.coefficients)}.
  - Chebyshev coefficients row {i} must have n_pressure={self.n_pressure} columns, got {len(row)}.
  - Chebyshev coefficient at ({i}, {j}) must be finite, got {value}.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Unit | Allowed values | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_temperature` | integer | yes |  |  |  | >= 1 |  |
| `n_pressure` | integer | yes |  |  |  | >= 1 |  |
| `tmin_k` | number \| null | no | `null` | K |  | > 0 |  |
| `tmax_k` | number \| null | no | `null` | K |  | > 0 |  |
| `pmin_bar` | number \| null | no | `null` | bar |  | > 0 |  |
| `pmax_bar` | number \| null | no | `null` | bar |  | > 0 |  |

Rules:

- **ChebyshevUpload.validate_grid** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  Mirror ``CalculationWithResultsPayload.validate_result_matches_type``
  for the ``irc_result`` / ``path_search_result`` / ``scan_result``
  fields. The base ``CalculationIn`` has no result-block matrix to
  validate, and the adapter uses ``model_copy(update=...)`` which
  bypasses pydantic validators — so this is the only place where
  mismatched ``(type, irc_result|path_search_result|scan_result)``
  pairs reject as 422 before hitting the persistence seam.

  ``scan_result`` is bundle-only and persisted by the workflow via
  ``persist_calculation_scan`` after the calculation row is created;
  the primitive payload does not carry it.

- **ComputedReactionCalculationIn.validate_constraint_indices_union_unique** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Enforce constraint_index uniqueness across the union of
  top-level ``constraints`` and ``scan_result.constraints``.

  Both lists land in the same ``calculation_constraint`` table and
  share the ``(calculation_id, constraint_index)`` composite PK,
  so a duplicate would otherwise surface as an opaque DB error at
  flush time.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `literature` | [`LiteratureUploadRequest`](#model-tckdb-schemas-literature-literatureuploadrequest) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `software_release` | [`SoftwareReleaseRef`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-refs-softwarereleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `analysis_software_release` | [`SoftwareReleaseRef`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-refs-softwarereleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |

| `species` | array of [`BundleSpeciesIn`](#model-tckdb-schemas-workflows-computed-reaction-upload-bundlespeciesin) | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `reversible` | boolean | no | `true` |  |  |  |  |
| `reaction_family` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `reaction_family_source_note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `reactant_keys` | array of string | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `product_keys` | array of string | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `transition_state` | [`BundleTransitionStateIn`](#model-tckdb-schemas-workflows-computed-reaction-upload-bundletransitionstatein) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `kinetics` | array of [`BundleKineticsIn`](#model-tckdb-schemas-workflows-computed-reaction-upload-bundlekineticsin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `atom_map` | [`ReactionAtomMapIn`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-reaction-atom-map-reactionatommapin) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Which atom of each reactant and product is which atom of the transition state. Supplied by the depositor and never derived here: TCKDB does not run a mapping algorithm, because several chemically distinct maps are usually consistent with the same reactants and products and choosing one by algorithm would manufacture provenance (ADR 0011). Optional — a reaction deposited without one succeeds and returns a 'reaction_atom_map_absent' upload warning, because an unmapped reaction is incomplete rather than false. Requires a transition state: both legs of the map run toward the saddle point. |

Rules:

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_atom_map** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Refuse a self-contradictory atom map; accept an incomplete one.

  Runs here rather than on a nested model because the map spans the
  reaction's participant slots, every participant's geometry, and the
  transition state's geometry — the same reason
  ``validate_ts_validation_evidence`` sits at this level.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_ts_validation_evidence** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Check TS evidence against the bundle's reaction and TS geometry.

  Participant/atom completeness needs the reaction's participants, their
  declared kinds and the TS atom count, none of which the nested TS model
  can see.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_reaction_family** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - reaction_family_source_note requires reaction_family.
  - reaction_family_source_note is required when reaction_family is not a supported canonical family.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_unique_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Species keys must be unique.
  - Calculation keys must be globally unique.
  - Geometry keys must be globally unique.
  - Conformer keys must be unique within species '{sp.key}'.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_species_key_refs** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Reaction references species key '{key}' which is not defined in the species list.
  - Kinetics fit references species key '{key}' which is not defined in the species list.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.validate_calculation_key_refs** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Validate every local-key reference to a calculation resolves.

  Covers the three cross-reference surfaces introduced for the
  producer-controlled provenance work:

  * ``CalculationIn.depends_on[].parent_calculation_key`` — must
    name a calculation defined elsewhere in the bundle, and must
    not equal the calculation it sits on (no self-edges).
  * ``BundleKineticsIn.source_calculations[].calculation_key`` —
    must name a calculation defined in the bundle.

  Per-key uniqueness is enforced separately by
  ``validate_unique_keys``; this validator only checks that every
  reference resolves into the bundle's calc namespace.

- **ComputedReactionUploadRequest.normalize_family** (field validator (after) on `reaction_family, reaction_family_source_note`; adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `reaction_family`, `reaction_family_source_note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

Use this for scheme-backed corrections such as AEC totals (application_role=aec_total) and BAC totals (application_role=bac_total). Frequency-scale-factor corrections still belong on thermo/statmech blocks where their source calc lives. ``source_conformer_key`` resolves against this bundle's conformer keys. |

Rules:

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_unique_conformer_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - conformers must have unique keys.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys_global** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Calc keys are GLOBAL across the bundle.

  Thermo source links and applied-correction source links reference
  any calc from any conformer; per-conformer scoping would force
  every reference to be a (conformer_key, calculation_key) tuple.
  Producers that want disambiguation can prefix keys
  (``conf0_opt``, ``conf1_opt``).

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_dependency_keys_resolve** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Every ``depends_on`` edge must name a calculation this bundle declares.

  Answers with the same code and the same ``context`` keys as
  ``app.workflows.computed_species``'s seam does for the identical
  mistake, so a depositor cannot tell which layer caught them
  (ADR 0017). The prose is unchanged from before it had a code.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Refuse frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008).

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_thermo_source_keys_resolve** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - thermo.source_calculations references undefined calculation_key '{sc.calculation_key}'.
  - thermo.applied_energy_corrections[{i}].source_calculation_key references undefined calculation_key '{ac.source_calculation_key}'.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_statmech_source_keys_resolve** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - statmech.source_calculations references undefined calculation_key '{sc.calculation_key}'.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_statmech_torsion_scan_keys_resolve** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - statmech.torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' references undefined calculation_key.
  - statmech.torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' must reference a scan-type calculation.

- **ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest.validate_top_level_applied_correction_source_keys_resolve** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Top-level applied corrections may reference any calc in the
  bundle's global calc-key namespace (mirrors the thermo path).

It is the conformer namespace's counterpart to ``ConformerCalculationIn.key``, and it is deliberately not ``label``: a label is a human tag that also participates in conformer-group matching, so renaming it for grouping reasons would silently break a correction reference, and a depositor who has no label has no way to point at their own conformer. Rules:

- **ConformerUploadRequest.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`, `label`, `conformer_key`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Conformer upload calculation keys must be unique within the request.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_statmech_calculation_keys_resolve** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Every statmech calc reference must name a calculation declared here.

  The conformer upload has no other calc-key namespace to fall back
  on, so an unrecognised key can only be a mistake. Refusing it is
  the difference between a 422 the depositor can fix and a
  provenance link that silently never existed.

  The code is ``statmech_calculation_key_undeclared`` because that is
  what ``app.services.statmech_resolution`` answers when the same
  typo survives to the write path — this route reaches that seam, and
  ADR 0017 says the depositor must not be able to tell which of the
  two caught them.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_primary_calculation_not_linked_twice** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  One link per (calculation, role), counting the implicit one.

  ``uploaded_calculation_role`` already links the primary
  calculation. Naming that same calculation again with the same role
  in ``source_calculations`` asks for two rows with one primary key,
  which the database refuses — better said here, where the message
  can name the field, than as a 500 mid-transaction.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_additional_calculation_types** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Additional calculation type '{calc.type.value}' is not allowed. Expected one of: {', '.join((t.value for t in sorted(_ALLOWED_ADDITIONAL_TYPES, key=lambda t: t.value)))}.

- **ConformerUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Refuse frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008).

| `source_calculations` | array of [`StatmechSourceCalcIn`](#model-tckdb-schemas-statmech-bits-statmechsourcecalcin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |

Rules:

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`, `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_electronic_levels** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - electronic_levels level_index values must be unique.

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Reject duplicate links the way the sibling paths already do.

  ``statmech_source_calculation`` is keyed on
  ``(statmech_id, calculation_id, role)``, so a repeated pair was a
  primary-key violation surfacing as a 500. The bundle and
  standalone statmech uploads validate this; the conformer path
  did not.

  The tuple carries a second discriminator alongside the key, read
  reflectively because this class is also the payload the *backend*
  hands the statmech resolution service — and the standalone
  statmech upload's entries are a subclass that may name a
  calculation by ``existing_calculation_id`` instead of by key.
  Without it, every such entry collapses to ``(None, role)`` and two
  genuinely different calculations sharing a role — one rotor scan
  per torsion, all of them ``role='scan'`` — are refused as a
  duplicate. Nothing changes for a payload built from this package:
  ``StatmechSourceCalcIn`` has no such attribute, so the second
  element is always ``None`` and the rule is the pair it always was.

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  One rotor per index, as the sibling upload paths already require.

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

<a id="model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-calculation-freqresultpayload"></a>

### `FreqResultPayload`

`tckdb_schemas.fragments.calculation`. Used by: [`ComputedSpeciesUploadRequest`](#surface-computedspeciesuploadrequest), [`ConformerUploadRequest`](#surface-conformeruploadrequest), [`StatmechUploadRequest`](#surface-statmechuploadrequest), [`ThermoUploadRequest`](#surface-thermouploadrequest), [`TransitionStateUploadRequest`](#surface-transitionstateuploadrequest), [`TransportUploadRequest`](#surface-transportuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#surface-contributionbundlev0).

Optional inline result for a frequency calculation.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Unit | Allowed values | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_imag` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Number of imaginary frequencies. |
| `imag_freq_cm1` | number \| null | no | `null` | cm^-1 |  |  | Value of the imaginary frequency in cm⁻¹. |
| `zpe_hartree` | number \| null | no | `null` | hartree |  |  | Zero-point energy in hartree. |
| `modes` | array of [`FrequencyModePayload`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-calculation-frequencymodepayload) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional per-mode frequency rows. When supplied, ``mode_index`` values must be unique within the payload, and the count of imaginary modes must agree with ``n_imag`` if both are present. |
| `reaction_coordinate_mode_index` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  |  | >= 1 | ``mode_index`` of the mode the depositor designates the reaction coordinate. ADR 0012 makes this the contract that replaces the old ``n_imag == 1`` gate: a transition state with more than one imaginary mode is accepted only if it says which one is the barrier and is removed from the partition function. Meaningless on a minimum, and refused there. |

Rules:

- **FreqResultPayload.validate_modes_consistency** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - mode_index values must be unique within a freq result. Index {', '.join((str(i) for i in duplicates))} appears more than once, so the list does not say which row is which mode and a consumer reading it cannot reconstruct the spectrum ({W_FREQ_MODE_INDEX_NOT_UNIQUE}). Renumber the modes to the ESS's own 1-based ordering.
  - n_imag={self.n_imag} does not match imaginary mode count {imaginary_count} in modes. The scalar the ESS printed and the frequency list deposited beside it are the same claim made twice, and a record that makes it two ways tells a consumer reading the summary something different from one reading the evidence ({W_FREQ_N_IMAG_DISAGREES_WITH_MODES}). Deposit the complete signed frequency list, or omit modes entirely -- absence is incompleteness, which is accepted, and only contradiction is refused.

- **FreqResultPayload.validate_reaction_coordinate_designation** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  The designated reaction coordinate must be an imaginary mode.

  Checked here rather than in
  :func:`~tckdb_schemas.stationary_point.evaluate_transition_state_frequency`
  because it is a statement about the payload's internal
  consistency, not about the chemistry: an index naming a real mode
  or naming nothing at all is a malformed record whatever kind of
  stationary point it describes.

| `degeneracy_convention` | `KineticsDegeneracyConvention` (enum) | no | `"unknown"` |  | KineticsDegeneracyConvention: `already_applied`, `not_applied`, `unknown` |  | Whether degeneracy is already included in the rate. |
| `tunneling_model` | `TunnelingModel` (enum) \| null | no | `null` |  | TunnelingModel: `none`, `wigner`, `eckart`, `sct`, `other` |  | Optional tunneling model label. |
| `interpretation_assignments` | array of [`KineticsInterpretationAssignmentUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-kineticsinterpretationassignmentupload) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `tunneling_application` | [`KineticsTunnelingApplicationUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-kineticstunnelingapplicationupload) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `pressure_context` | `PressureContext` (enum) \| null | no | `null` |  | PressureContext: `high_p_limit`, `apparent_at_pressure`, `pressure_dependent` |  |  |
| `pressure_bar` | number \| null | no | `null` | bar |  | > 0 |  |
| `falloff` | [`FalloffUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-falloffupload) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `third_body_efficiencies` | array of [`ThirdBodyEfficiencyUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-thirdbodyefficiencyupload) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `plog_entries` | array of [`PlogEntryUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-plogentryupload) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `arrhenius_entries` | array of [`MultiArrheniusEntryUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-multiarrheniusentryupload) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `chebyshev` | [`ChebyshevUpload`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-kinetics-upload-chebyshevupload) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional free-text note. |

Rules:

- **KineticsUploadRequest.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_pressure_context** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - pressure_context='apparent_at_pressure' requires pressure_bar.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_reported_ea_pair** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - reported_ea and reported_ea_units must both be provided or both omitted.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_temperature_range** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - tmin_k must be less than or equal to tmax_k.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_multi_arrhenius** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Bind ``multi_arrhenius`` to its sum-of-terms child rows (DR-0036).

  A DUPLICATE channel is a sum of at least two modified-Arrhenius
  terms; the scalar ``a`` must stay unset because the coefficient lives
  in the child entries, and the entry indices must be unique.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_a_uncertainty_kind** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - a_uncertainty and a_uncertainty_kind must both be provided or both omitted.
  - Multiplicative a_uncertainty must be >= 1.0 (factor f, with the true value within [A/f, A*f]).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_third_body_is_meaningful** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  PLOG and Chebyshev are never third-body reactions.

  Both parameterizations already carry the full pressure dependence, so
  CHEMKIN does not admit a ``+M`` third-body designation on them.
  Accepting the flag was not merely cosmetic: it made
  :meth:`_main_line_molecularity` raise the expected A-unit order by
  one, so a PLOG entry carrying the CORRECT units for its molecularity
  was rejected while one carrying the units of the next order up was
  accepted.

  Declared ahead of the A-unit validators so the actionable message
  wins: validators run in definition order, and the inflated-order unit
  error would otherwise mask the real cause.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_a_units_vs_molecularity** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `validate_a_units_for_molecularity`: Raise ValueError if a_units is incompatible with the reaction molecularity.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_arrhenius_entries_a_units** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Every summed ``multi_arrhenius`` term is the SAME reaction rate, so
  each term's ``a_units`` must match the main-line molecularity (DR-0036).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_plog_entries_a_units** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Each PLOG pressure entry's A is the reaction's rate at that pressure,
  so its ``a_units`` shares the main-line molecularity (DR-0032 Part C).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_falloff_low_a_units** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  The low-pressure-limit k0 Arrhenius is by definition one order higher
  than k∞, so ``falloff.low_a_units`` validates at ``len(reactants) + 1``
  regardless of ``is_third_body`` (DR-0032 Part B).

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_model_scientific_content** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  A fit must carry parameters for the declared functional form.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.default_tunneling_model_from_application** (model validator (before); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Fill the label from the evidence block at parse time.

  Normalisation belongs in a *before* validator. Doing it in an
  after-validator mutated an already-constructed model, so the parsed
  object silently diverged from the validated one.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_tunneling_declaration_agrees** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Cross-check the tunneling declaration against its evidence block.

  ``tunneling_model`` is a *label*: a reported attribute of the rate, of
  the same kind a mechanism file or a paper's methods section carries.
  A literature rate whose authors state "Eckart tunneling was applied"
  genuinely has no imaginary frequency, no barriers and no artifact for
  the depositor to attach, and neither does a rate imported from a
  CHEMKIN mechanism. Demanding typed evidence for a label would force
  exactly the invention this schema exists to prevent, so its absence is
  reported as an upload warning instead.

  ``tunneling_application`` is *evidence*. When present it must be
  internally complete (enforced on that model) and must agree with the
  label it is offered for.

- **KineticsUploadRequest.validate_interpretation_content** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  An interpretation set, once offered, must be complete.

  Supplying ``interpretation_assignments`` is the claim "this rate was
  built from these partition functions in this database". A *partial*
  set is worse than none: it looks like provenance while leaving the
  unnamed participants entirely unaccounted for. So the completeness
  requirement attaches to that claim, not to ``scientific_origin``.

  ``scientific_origin='computed'`` means only "this number came from a
  calculation" — it does not mean the calculation's partition functions
  live here. A rate read out of a CHEMKIN mechanism, or an Arkane TST
  result deposited without its statmech, is computed in origin and
  carries no assignments; rejecting it would lose a real record. Its
  lack of assignments is reported as an upload warning instead.

  ``participant_index`` is bounded here rather than only at the
  persistence seam, so an out-of-range slot is a 422 and not a late
  500-shaped failure.

- **KineticsUploadRequest._normalize_tunneling** (field validator (before) on `tunneling_model`; adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_tunneling_model` to `tunneling_model`: Coerce a producer-supplied tunneling model to a canonical token.

| `states` | array of [`NetworkStateIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-networkstatein) | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `channels` | array of [`NetworkChannelIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-networkchannelin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `solve` | [`NetworkSolveIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-networksolvein) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |

Rules:

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.normalize_text** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `name`, `description`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_unique_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Ensure all local keys are unique within their respective lists,
  and that calculation/geometry keys are globally unique.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_key_references** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Ensure all cross-references point to defined keys.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_unique_channels** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Ensure channel identities are stable while allowing parallel paths.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_unique_channel_kinetics** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Ensure no duplicate channel_kinetics within one payload.

  Uniqueness is keyed by ``(source_state_key, sink_state_key,
  model_kind)``: one channel may legitimately carry *both* a Chebyshev
  and a PLOG parameterization of the same k(T,P) (multiple
  parameterizations of one network coexisting on the same channel — the
  model imposes no ``(channel, solve)`` uniqueness). What remains user
  error, and is rejected here, is two entries of the *same* model_kind on
  one channel (two Chebyshevs or two PLOGs), which would silently write
  two redundant ``NetworkKinetics`` rows for one (channel, solve, kind).
  Multiple rows per (channel, solve) across separate uploads remain
  legitimate under append-only semantics.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_mechanistic_channel_evidence** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - channel '{channel.key}' microreaction_paths must be unique by reaction and TS.
  - state_energies must provide exactly one energy for every network state.
  - channel_barriers must provide exactly one barrier for every saddle-point channel path, and none for a barrierless path.
  - channel '{channel.key}' references undefined micro_reaction_key '{reaction_key}'.
  - channel '{channel.key}' references undefined transition_state_key '{ts_key}'.
  - channel '{channel.key}' TS '{ts_key}' does not belong to micro reaction '{reaction_key}'.
  - state_energies references undefined source_calculation_key.
  - energy_transfer references undefined state_key.
  - energy_transfer references undefined collider_species_key.
  - channel_barriers references undefined source_calculation_key.
  - energy_transfer must cover exactly one entry per (well state, bath-gas collider) pair, or declare a single scope='network_wide' entry if the run specified one model for the whole network. Missing: {missing}. Unexpected: {extra}.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_well_skipping_channels** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  A well-skipping declaration must be supported by the topology.

  The scientific content of ``mechanism='well_skipping'`` is a claim
  about the network: the endpoints are *not* directly connected by an
  elementary step, and the flux reaches the sink by traversing one or
  more energized wells. Both halves are checkable against the
  ``micro_reactions`` and ``states`` already in this payload, so the
  declaration is verified rather than trusted — the backend still
  manufactures no evidence, it only reads the evidence the producer
  supplied.

  Bimolecular and termolecular configurations are reservoirs in the
  master equation: flux that reaches one has separated into products.
  Only a *well* can be an energized intermediate, so intermediates on the
  path are required to be wells.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_no_unused_species** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Reject if a species is defined but never referenced anywhere.

- **NetworkPDepUploadRequest.validate_states_connected** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Ensure all states form one connected component via channels.

  A PDep network must be a single connected component — disconnected
  subnetworks are not supported. If channels are provided, checks
  that every state is reachable from every other state through the
  channel graph. If no channels exist, skips this check (channels
  may be inferred later by the backend).

<a id="model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-networksolvein"></a>

### `NetworkSolveIn`

`app.schemas.workflows.network_pdep_upload`. Used by: [`NetworkPDepUploadRequest`](#surface-networkpdepuploadrequest).

Master-equation solve configuration and provenance.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Unit | Allowed values | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `NetworkSolveKind` (enum) | no | `"computed"` |  | NetworkSolveKind: `computed`, `reported` |  | Whether the master equation was solved here (``computed``, the default and preferred form) or the k(T,P) were transcribed from a publication (``reported``). A ``reported`` solve is not held to the state-energy, channel-barrier or energy-transfer coverage rules — it holds none of those inputs — and must supply ``literature`` instead. See ADR 0010. |
| `me_method` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | ME solution method. |
| `interpolation_model` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Interpolation model for the ME solution. |
| `tmin_k` | number | yes |  | K |  | > 0 | Minimum temperature in K for the ME solve. |
| `tmax_k` | number | yes |  | K |  | > 0 | Maximum temperature in K for the ME solve. |
| `pmin_bar` | number | yes |  | bar |  | > 0 | Minimum pressure in bar for the ME solve. |
| `pmax_bar` | number | yes |  | bar |  | > 0 | Maximum pressure in bar for the ME solve. |
| `grain_size_cm_inv` | number \| null | no | `null` | cm^-1 |  |  | Energy grain size in cm⁻¹. |
| `grain_count` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  |  | >= 1 | Number of energy grains. |
| `emax_kj_mol` | number \| null | no | `null` | kJ/mol |  |  | Maximum energy in kJ/mol for the ME solve. |
| `literature` | [`LiteratureUploadRequest`](#model-tckdb-schemas-literature-literatureuploadrequest) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional literature submission payload. Required when ``kind='reported'``. |
| `software_release` | [`SoftwareReleaseRef`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-refs-softwarereleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional software provenance reference. |
| `workflow_tool_release` | [`WorkflowToolReleaseRef`](#model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-refs-workflowtoolreleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional workflow-tool provenance reference. |
| `bath_gas` | array of [`BathGasIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-bathgasin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  | Bath gas composition. |
| `energy_transfer` | array of [`EnergyTransferIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-energytransferin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  | Energy transfer model parameters — either one ``per_well`` entry per (well, bath collider) pair, or a single ``network_wide`` entry. |
| `state_energies` | array of [`StateEnergyIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-stateenergyin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `channel_barriers` | array of [`ChannelBarrierIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-channelbarrierin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |
| `source_calculations` | array of [`SolveSourceCalculationIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-solvesourcecalculationin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  | Calculations used in this solve, by local key and role. |
| `channel_kinetics` | array of [`NetworkKineticsIn`](#model-app-schemas-workflows-network-pdep-upload-networkkineticsin) | no | `[]` |  |  |  | Fitted phenomenological k(T,P) for channels, each referencing its channel by ``(source_state_key, sink_state_key)``. |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  | Optional free-text note. |

Rules:

- **NetworkSolveIn.normalize_text** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `me_method`, `interpolation_model`, `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **NetworkSolveIn.validate_ranges** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - tmin_k must be less than or equal to tmax_k.
  - pmin_bar must be less than or equal to pmax_bar.

- **NetworkSolveIn.validate_unique_bath_gas** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Bath gas entries must reference distinct species_key values.

- **NetworkSolveIn.validate_kind_requirements** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Hold a computed solve to the master-equation inputs it must have.

  These are the requirements ``min_length`` used to carry. They move
  here because they apply to one member of ``kind`` and not the other: a
  computed solve is a claim that the master equation was solved in this
  database, and a solve with no state energies and no source
  calculations does not support it. A reported solve makes no such
  claim, so the same absence is the expected shape rather than a defect
  (ADR 0010).

  What a reported solve *must* have is the mirror image: the publication
  it was transcribed from, and at least one k(T,P) — a record that
  reports nothing contradicts its own kind. Both are definitional, so
  both block under ADR 0008. The completeness limitation that *is* an
  expectation rather than a definition — that nobody can re-derive these
  rates — warns instead, in
  ``collect_network_solve_kind_warnings``.

- **NetworkSolveIn.validate_bath_composition_and_state_energies** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - state_energies must be unique by state_key.
  - energy_transfer entries must all share one scope: either every entry is per_well, or there is a single network_wide entry. Mixing the two leaves it undefined which wells the network-wide model applies to.
  - a network_wide energy_transfer declaration is a single entry; supplying more than one says nothing about which applies where.
  - energy_transfer entries must be unique by (scope, state_key, collider_species_key).
  - bath_gas mole fractions must sum to 1.0 within 1e-9.

- **ReactionAtomMapIn.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Trim ``note`` and collapse a blank one to ``None``.

  Declared before the ``inferred`` rule below so that rule sees the
  normalised value: ``note='   '`` is not the name of an algorithm, and
  without this it would satisfy "an inferred map says what inferred it"
  while carrying nothing at all — the anonymous inferred map ADR 0011
  exists to prevent, admitted through whitespace.

  An inferred map must say what inferred it.

  Definitional, therefore blocking. ADR 0011 permits inference only as a
  *labelled and separable* thing; an inferred map whose origin is
  anonymous is one careless consumer away from being read as a human
  assertion.

<a id="model-tckdb-schemas-fragments-reaction-atom-map-reactionatommapparticipantin"></a>

### `ReactionAtomMapParticipantIn`

`tckdb_schemas.fragments.reaction_atom_map`. Used by: [`ComputedReactionUploadRequest`](#surface-computedreactionuploadrequest).

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Unit | Allowed values | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `side` | `ReactionRole` (enum) | yes |  |  | ReactionRole: `reactant`, `product` |  | Which leg this participant sits on. |
| `species_key` | string | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 | Bundle-local key of the species this participant is. |
| `participant_index` | integer | yes |  |  |  | >= 1 | 1-based position of this participant on its side. Required because the same species may appear twice on one side (``2 CH3 → C2H6``) and the two copies map to different saddle-point atoms. |
| `geometry_key` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | length >= 1 | Bundle-local key of the geometry the atom indices count into. Named explicitly; see the module docstring. Omitted, and only omitted, by a participant with no atoms: there are no indices to count, and naming a geometry a participant does not have would be the implicit-indexing failure this fragment exists to prevent, written explicitly. |
| `atom_to_ts` | object (integer -> integer) | yes |  |  |  |  | ``{atom index in this participant's geometry: atom index in the transition-state geometry}``. Both sides 1-based. Empty **only** for a participant that has no atoms — a free electron. That is a claim ("this participant is made of nothing"), not an omission: a depositor who mapped none of a molecule's atoms leaves the participant out of the map entirely, and the incompleteness warning says so. |

Rules:

- **ReactionAtomMapParticipantIn.validate_geometry_is_named_exactly_when_indices_exist** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Indices need a geometry; a participant with none must not name one.

  Both directions are refused because both are unreadable. An index with
  no geometry beside it identifies a position in an ordering the reader
  has to guess at, which is the whole reason ADR 0011 chose
  geometry-relative indexing over canonical ordering. A geometry beside
  no indices is the reverse claim, from a participant that by its own
  account has no atoms in that geometry to point at -- a free electron
  has no geometry anywhere in the deposit.

- **ReactionAtomMapParticipantIn.validate_indices_are_one_based** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - atom_map participant '{self.species_key}' [{self.side.value} {self.participant_index}] uses 1-based atom indices on both sides.

Rules:

- **SoftwareReleaseRef.normalize_optional_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `version`, `revision`, `build`, `notes`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **SoftwareReleaseRef.normalize_composite_version** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Warn on, and deterministically normalise, a composite ``version``.

  Never refuses (issue #305 follow-up: refusing broke real ARC
  ingestion outright -- five real payloads carried
  ``version="ORCA 6.0.0"`` under a stale ``name="gaussian"``, and
  every one of them was a correct deposit of a producer bug this
  archive has no business rejecting). Instead:

  1. If ``version`` has no internal whitespace, it is not a banner
     shape at all -- return silently. This also deliberately leaves
     the unrelated literal string ``"None"`` alone (86 rows on the
     ARC fixtures; a different defect -- something serialised
     Python's ``None`` through ``str()`` upstream -- with no comma,
     space, or structure a version/revision split could act on).

  2. Split off the leading whitespace-delimited token. If it does
     **not** case-insensitively match the declared ``name``, this
     is the mismatch case: the version is the observed fact (it
     came from parsing a real ESS banner) and the name is the
     inherited one (ARC's own default/previous value bleeding into
     a per-calculation software_release). Leave both fields
     completely untouched and warn
     ``W_SOFTWARE_RELEASE_NAME_LOOKS_WRONG`` -- stripping here would
     manufacture a release that never ran.

  3. If it *does* match, strip the leading name and try to split a
     trailing ``", Revision <label>"`` suffix out of what remains.
     If the depositor already supplied their own ``revision``,
     do not choose between it and the one embedded in ``version``
     -- leave both fields exactly as declared and warn. Otherwise
     write ``version``/``revision`` from the split (or just the
     stripped ``version`` when there is no revision suffix) and
     warn ``W_SOFTWARE_RELEASE_VERSION_IS_COMPOSITE``.

  A successful split also appends a short provenance note to
  ``notes`` recording the verbatim string as declared -- see the
  note on ``notes`` below for why here and not
  ``calculation.observed_software_banner``.

- **SoftwareReleaseRef.normalize_name** (field validator (after) on `name`; adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_required_text` to `name`: Trim required text inputs and reject blank values.

  make a structure invisible to elemental balance; a ``molecule``
  carrying ``[e-]`` would be handed to RDKit, which cannot parse it.

- **SpeciesEntryIdentityPayload.normalize_identity_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

- **SpeciesEntryIdentityPayload.normalize_smiles** (field validator (after) on `smiles`; adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_required_text` to `smiles`: Trim required text inputs and reject blank values.

  - Statmech torsion_index values must be unique within the bundle.

- **StatmechInBundle.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.normalize_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`, `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_electronic_levels** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - electronic_levels level_index values must be unique.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Statmech calculations must have unique keys.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Refuse inline frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). The inline
  calculations are scoped to this upload's species entry, so the
  declared kind and the parsed ``n_imag`` are both present here.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_source_calculation_keys_exist** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Every *local* citation must name a calculation this request declares.

  Chained citations (``existing_calculation_id``) carry no key and
  are skipped here on purpose: the row they name was deposited by an
  earlier request, so this payload cannot possibly declare it. They
  are not thereby unchecked — existence, owner-consistency and
  role/type compatibility are all enforced against the database in
  :func:`app.services.statmech_resolution.resolve_or_create_statmech`,
  which is the only place that can check them.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Refuse a repeated link, whichever way the calculation is named.

  ``statmech_source_calculation`` is keyed on ``(statmech_id,
  calculation_id, role)``, so a duplicate is a primary-key violation
  surfacing as a 500. The reference is now two-valued, so the
  uniqueness tuple carries both halves — the same shape thermo's
  ``ThermoSourceCalculationIn`` uniqueness check uses.

  One duplicate this cannot see: the same calculation cited once by
  inline key and once by id. That is impossible in practice, because
  an inline calculation is minted by this request and so has no id an
  earlier request could have handed out; the database's own primary
  key remains the backstop either way.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Torsion indices must be unique within a statmech upload.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_torsion_scan_calculation_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' does not reference a declared calculation.

  Default an omitted ``phase`` to ``gas``, for computed records only.

  Only ``scientific_origin: computed`` gets the default, and only when
  ``phase`` is omitted; an explicit ``null`` is kept as unknown.
  ``reference_pressure_bar`` is never defaulted, for any origin.

- **ThermoInBundle.validate_temperature_range** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

- **ThermoInBundle.validate_has_scientific_content** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Thermo block must include at least one of: a scalar thermo value (h298_kj_mol, s298_j_mol_k or enthalpy_formation_0k_kj_mol), a NASA block, or one or more thermo points.

<a id="model-app-schemas-workflows-thermoml-upload-thermomluploadrequest"></a>

### `ThermoMLUploadRequest`

`app.schemas.workflows.thermoml_upload`. Used by: [`ThermoMLUploadRequest`](#surface-thermomluploadrequest).

One ThermoML XML document, uploaded directly (not from the NIST bulk archive — that path is the ``--archive``/``--doi`` CLI only).

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Unit | Allowed values | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | string | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1, length <= 255 | Provenance metadata only — recorded verbatim (as ``f"upload:{filename}"``) in the custody row's ``mapping_report_json["source_label"]``. Never used as a storage path (the object store is content-addressed by SHA-256) and never used as a fallback ``raw_uri`` the way an archive member path is (see ``app.services.thermoml_cp_import._raw_uri_for``'s ``allow_member_path_fallback``) — it is a display label, not a retrievable location. |
| `content_base64` | string | yes |  |  |  | length >= 1 | Base64-encoded ThermoML XML bytes. |
| `doi` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | length <= 255 | The article's own DOI, if the depositor wants to assert it explicitly. Optional — when omitted, the DOI is taken from the file's own ``Citation/sDOI`` element, if present. Supplying one that disagrees with the file's own ``sDOI`` is a refusal (``thermoml_doi_conflict``), never a silent override. |
| `rights` | [`DepositRights`](#model-tckdb-schemas-rights-depositrights) | yes |  |  |  |  | The depositor's deposit-time license agreement. Required — deliberately **not** optional like ``DepositRights`` on every other upload schema. Every other upload route can fall back on "attested later, at release time" because the underlying science already exists in TCKDB under someone's authority; this route's whole content *is* a third-party document the depositor is asserting the right to submit, and unlike the CLI's ``--archive`` path there is no NIST/TRC ``source_terms`` to stand on instead. Omitting it is refused by ordinary Pydantic field-requiredness (422, the same mechanism every other required field on every other schema in this codebase already uses — not a new bespoke refusal). Recorded as an ordinary ``depositor_agreement`` attestation, never ``source_terms``. |

Rules:

- **ThermoMLUploadRequest._validate_filename** (field validator (after) on `filename`; can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - filename must not contain path separators or '..'

- **ThermoMLUploadRequest._normalize_doi** (field validator (after) on `doi`; adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Trim ``doi``; a blank DOI is treated as absent.

The only accepted value is formation_298k. Required when the record carries any enthalpy or Gibbs-energy content and refused when it carries none; never defaulted or inferred. |

| `nasa` | [`ThermoNASACreate`](#model-tckdb-schemas-thermo-thermonasacreate) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `nasa9_intervals` | array of [`ThermoNASA9IntervalCreate`](#model-tckdb-schemas-thermo-thermonasa9intervalcreate) | no | `[]` |  |  |  |  |

Rules:

- **ThermoUploadRequest.normalize_text_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.apply_computed_origin_defaults** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its docstring):

  Fill the ``phase`` default only for computed uploads.

  A computed QC record's thermo values come from an ideal-gas
  rigid-rotor/harmonic-oscillator treatment, so ``phase`` defaults to
  ``gas`` when the uploader omits it. For experimental/literature/
  estimated origins the field stays ``None`` unless explicitly
  provided — defaulting it would silently stamp e.g. a
  condensed-phase literature value as ``gas``.

  ``reference_pressure_bar`` is NEVER defaulted, for any origin
  (decided 2026-09-24, issue #529): an omitted pressure is stored as not
  stated, never assumed to be 1 bar or 1 atm.

  Explicit values (including an explicit ``None``) are honored:
  ``model_fields_set`` distinguishes "omitted" from "provided".

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_temperature_range** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - tmin_k must be less than or equal to tmax_k.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_unique_points** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Thermo points must be unique by temperature_k.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - Thermo calculations must have unique keys.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Refuse inline frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). The inline
  calculations are scoped to this upload's species entry, so the
  declared kind and the parsed ``n_imag`` are both present here.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_source_calculation_keys_exist** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Every source_calculations[*].calculation_key, when provided, must
  reference a calculation declared in this upload. Entries that use
  ``existing_calculation_id`` instead are skipped — those are resolved
  against the database in the workflow layer.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its refusal messages):

  - source_calculations must be unique by (calculation_key, existing_calculation_id, role).

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_applied_correction_source_calc_keys** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Every applied_energy_corrections[*].source_calculation_key, when
  provided, must reference a calculation declared in this upload. This
  prevents silent provenance loss where a correction would otherwise
  persist with a NULL source_calculation_id.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_energy_level_requires_no_statmech_link** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  ``energy_level_of_theory`` is meaningless once a statmech basis
  is linked: the record's levels then come entirely from that
  statmech record (R6), and there is no local 'opt'/'sp' link left
  for this field to be checked against. Refuse the combination
  outright rather than silently ignoring one of the two — the
  depositor almost certainly meant one or the other.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_group_additivity_origin** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  A GA breakdown may only attach to an ``estimated`` thermo record.

  Group additivity *is* the estimation method; attaching it to a
  computed / experimental / literature record would misrepresent the
  record's scientific origin.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_has_scientific_content** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Reject uploads that carry only identity/provenance and no thermo data.

  At least one of: a scalar thermo value (``h298_kj_mol`` or
  ``s298_j_mol_k`` or ``enthalpy_formation_0k_kj_mol``), a NASA-7 polynomial block, a NASA-9 interval set,
  a Wilhoit block, or one or more tabulated thermo points must be
  present. Provenance-only fields such as ``literature``,
  ``software_release``, ``workflow_tool_release``, and ``note`` do not
  count.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_representation_consistency** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Enforce a single temperature-dependent *fit* representation.

  At most one fit form {nasa (NASA-7), nasa9_intervals, wilhoit} may be
  populated — mixing e.g. a NASA-9 fit and a Wilhoit fit on one thermo
  record is ambiguous. Tabulated ``points`` are NOT a fit: they may
  accompany a fit as auxiliary evidence, or stand alone (tabulated).
  When ``model_kind`` is supplied it must match the primary
  representation (nasa7↔nasa, nasa9↔nasa9_intervals, wilhoit↔wilhoit,
  tabulated↔points-only, scalar↔none). When ``model_kind`` is None the
  backend infers it (a fit wins over points). NASA-9 interval indices
  must be unique and contiguous from 1.

| `dipole_debye` | number \| null | no | `null` | debye |  |  | Dipole moment in Debye. |

  Reject uploads that carry only identity/provenance and no transport data.

  At least one of ``sigma_angstrom``, ``epsilon_over_k_k``,
  ``dipole_debye``, ``polarizability_angstrom3``, or
  ``rotational_relaxation`` must be present. Provenance-only fields such
  as ``literature``, ``software_release``, ``workflow_tool_release``, and
  ``note`` do not count.

  A transport row carrying none of these is definitionally empty — it
  claims to be transport data while carrying no transport property — so
  this is a contract violation and blocks at upload, per ADR 0008
  (``docs/adr/0008-validation-tiers-definitions-block-expectations-warn.md``).
  The read-time counterpart is the backend's
  ``HardFailReason.no_transport_property_present``, which this check owns
  as the blocking tier; the trust label remains as a backstop for rows
  that entered by a non-upload path.

- **TransportUploadPayload.validate_lj_pair** (model validator (after); can refuse; from its docstring):

  Require Lennard-Jones sigma and epsilon/k to be provided together.

| `git_commit` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | length >= 1, length <= 40 |  |
| `release_date` | string (date) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |
| `notes` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |  |

Rules:

- **WorkflowToolReleaseRef.normalize_optional_fields** (model validator (after); adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_optional_text` to `version`, `git_commit`, `notes`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

- **WorkflowToolReleaseRef.normalize_name** (field validator (after) on `name`; adjusts values, no refusal in its own body; from its documented helpers it calls):

  - applies `normalize_required_text` to `name`: Trim required text inputs and reject blank values.

## Refusal code reference

Every code a producer route was traced to, plus every client-facing code in the catalogue whether traced or not. `Message` is the sentence written beside the code at its raise site, found by a static search and printed with `{placeholders}` for the parts filled in at run time; where the search finds none it says so rather than guessing.

<a id="code-ambiguous-conformer-selection-locator"></a>

#### `ambiguous_conformer_selection_locator`

- Status: 422; client-facing: yes; arrives as: coded_exception.
- Defined in: `backend/app/services/conformer_selection_locator.py`.
- Traced on: [`KineticsUploadRequest`](#surface-kineticsuploadrequest), [`ContributionBundleV0`](#surface-contributionbundlev0).
- Shape: relationship -- the body's `context` names the things involved.
- Message: not found by the static search.
- Note: Shape.relationship, and it was already meeting the obligation before there was a field to name it: the code says several rows matched and names none of them, while Discrimination.as_context reports match_count, differs_by, discriminator, discriminator_values and locator_can_express -- the things that differ, never their ids. So this entry needed a declaration, not a repair. It is also the first code to arrive after RELATIONSHIP_WORDS existed, and it arrived misclassified by omission: written before Shape was, it took the Shape.thing default and the word guard refused it on the merge. Nothing else would have -- the merge was textually clean. The 'several matched' half of a split; unknown_conformer_selection is the 'none matched' half, at 404. Both used to be one bare ValueError reading 'must resolve exactly one selection', so 422 validation_error with an empty context covered two opposite repairs -- deposit the missing row, versus say more about which row you meant. 422 and not 409 because every candidate exists: the world is consistent and the request is under-determined. context reports what actually differs across the candidates (discriminator, discriminator_values) and whether the locator has a field for it (locator_can_express), because 'be more specific' is only advice if there is something to add. For a long time there was not: the lookup filtered on all three locator fields, so candidates agreed on all three and could only differ by the conformer group, which the locator could not name -- every observed refusal reported locator_can_express=false, which was the evidence the locator needed widening. It has since been widened. The locator carries an optional conformer_group_ref, the field is filtered on when supplied, and this refusal now names it: discriminator=conformer_group_ref, locator_can_express=true, and discriminator_values listing the cg_ refs to choose between. The code, the status and every context key are unchanged -- what changed is that the advice can now be followed.

Both of its ownership comparisons were inline and raised a bare ValueError, so the mistake answered validation_error; both now call the shared guard. The three older call sites still cannot produce it -- they read from a key map built for the target's own owner -- but reachability is a property of the code, not of every site that raises it.
